description:
Maintainer-requested publish prep for the 7 kovan-* crates. Derived the real internal dependency graph via `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps` (no dev-dep edges among kovan-* crates):

  kovan-common (no internal deps)
  kovan-discovery    -> kovan-common
  kovan-codegen      -> kovan-common
  kovan-literature   -> kovan-common
  kovan-semantics    -> kovan-common, kovan-discovery
  kovan-metrics      -> kovan-discovery
  kovan (AGPL)       -> all 6 of the above

Batch 1 = the first 5 in a valid topological order that also respects crates.io's documented rate limit (docs/workspace-maintenance.md: burst of ~5 new crate NAMES, then ~1/10min): kovan-common, kovan-discovery, kovan-codegen, kovan-literature, kovan-semantics. All bumped 0.0.0 -> 0.0.1 (their own Cargo.toml `version` + the root [workspace.dependencies] pin, kept in sync per that doc's "drift" warning).

Also fixed a real gap found while prepping: none of the 6 kovan-* library crates (kovan itself excepted) had a per-crate LICENSE file -- every other published crate in this workspace does (workspace-maintenance.md: "a LICENSE at the workspace root does not ship"). Copied the root GPL-3.0 LICENSE into all 6. Also added the missing `repository.workspace = true` field to all 7 kovan-* crates' Cargo.toml (present on other workspace crates like outram-foam-basic-lib, was silently absent on every kovan-* one including `kovan` itself).

Verified:
- cargo check/test --release clean for all 5 batch-1 crates plus kovan-metrics/kovan (unbumped, confirm nothing broke).
- `cargo package --list -p kovan-common --allow-dirty`: clean contents, LICENSE included.
- `cargo publish -p kovan-common --dry-run --allow-dirty`: full verify + package + upload-dry-run succeeds (kovan-common has zero internal deps, so this is a real end-to-end check).
- `cargo publish -p kovan-discovery --dry-run --allow-dirty`: fails with the EXPECTED "no matching package named kovan-common found" (workspace-maintenance.md: "that is expected, not a packaging error") -- confirms discovery/codegen/literature/semantics genuinely cannot be verified until kovan-common is actually live.
- `cargo package --list --allow-dirty` for discovery/codegen/literature/semantics: clean contents, LICENSE included, nothing unexpected.

NOT YET DONE (explicitly out of scope for this bead -- prep only, not execution): actually running `cargo publish` (no --dry-run) for any crate. That is a real, irreversible action against the public registry and needs the maintainer's go-ahead per-crate, in order:
  1. kovan-common
  2. kovan-discovery
  3. kovan-codegen
  4. kovan-literature
  5. kovan-semantics
  (wait for crates.io's rate-limit cooldown / a 429's Retry-After)
  6. kovan-metrics (bump 0.0.0 -> 0.0.1 first, not yet done)
  (wait again if needed)
  7. kovan (bump 0.0.0 -> desired version first; also needs LICENSE already present -- confirmed AGPL text already correct)

kovan-metrics' version was deliberately left at 0.0.0 in this pass -- batch 2, not part of the "first 5" the maintainer asked for.

description:
crates/outram-foam-turbulence-lib has no usable wall functions, and the consequence is measured.

WHAT EXISTS: crates/outram-foam-turbulence-lib/src/wall_functions/mod.rs is the entire wall-function surface -- three free functions, y_plus (:37), u_tau (:50), nu_t_wall (:76). There is NO nutkWallFunction, kqRWallFunction, omegaWallFunction, epsilonWallFunction or nutUWallFunction implementation; those names appear only in prose (docs/model-reference.md:41, src/k_epsilon/mod.rs:59-60, README). The module doc admits it (:27-29): "These are standalone helper functions, not yet wired into any model as patch boundary conditions, and are untested."
Confirmed: a workspace-wide grep finds ZERO call sites for nu_t_wall / u_tau / y_plus outside the defining module, and the module contains ZERO #[test] functions.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE (re-run 2026-08-07, reproduced verbatim):
crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/tests/turbulence_coupling.rs, lid-driven cavity, genuinely Re = 100 (:234-235: 400 cells, U_lid = 1 m/s, nu = 1e-3 m^2/s, L = 0.1 m), Wilcox k-omega:
    nu_t after 0.5 s: min 2.5736e-1, max 3.3015e-1 m^2/s   (nu = 1.0e-3)
    => nu_t/nu = 257.4 to 330.2
    max |U_kOmega - U_laminar| = 2.249334e-1 m/s
A turbulent viscosity 257-330x the molecular value in a laminar Re=100 cavity is physically absurd and is the signature of a missing wall treatment.
(File the exact figure 257.4-330.2; the "260-330" recorded at turbulence_coupling.rs:46 and :264 rounds 257.4 up.)

SECOND DEFECT: the test PRINTS those values but asserts only finiteness and nu_t > 0 (:346-357). The magnitude is not gated, so a regression would not fail CI. Add a magnitude gate.

WORK:
1. Implement the standard wall functions as patch boundary conditions and wire them into the models.
2. Add a magnitude assertion to turbulence_coupling.rs so nu_t/nu in a laminar cavity is bounded.
3. Add unit tests for y_plus / u_tau / nu_t_wall, which currently have none.
title: outram-foam-turbulence-lib: wall functions missing — Re=100 cavity gives nu_t/nu = 257-330

description:
SteamGenerator (components/steam_generator.rs:19) has heat_exchanger: HeatExchanger (so inherits only that heat-transfer Area) and secondary_side: HemSteamCv. No envelope of its own.

Likely follows whatever HeatExchanger gets; wire the dependency accordingly.

Part of op-dt3.17. The digital-twin widget layer must derive a component's on-screen size from its REAL dimensions; the engine crate forbids new physics, so the dimension must exist here in tampines.

DO NOT use HemSteamCv::get_volume() as a size -- it is the thermodynamic control volume, caller-supplied and unvalidated, conventionally a 1 m3 dummy (get_ref_vol() returns exactly 1.0 m3). It describes the fluid parcel, not the machine.

Prefer explicit named dimensions where shape matters to the drawing; a single nominal Volume is acceptable where only a rough size correlation is wanted. Document units and valid ranges in the doc comment per the workspace human-interface rule, and keep uom types.
title: tampines SteamGenerator: add envelope dimensions
